title: Nonnegativity of Conditional Bit Distance
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol for length-$n$ set disjointness, and let $z$ be an achievable record of the transcript, special coordinate, Alice’s preceding bits, and Bob’s following bits. The total variation distance between the conditional law of Alice’s bit at the special coordinate on the fiber $Z=z$ and the uniform law on one bit is nonnegative.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol for length-$n$ disjointness
replaced:
Fix a positive integer $n$, a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for disjointness
inputs of length $n$, and an achievable value $z$ of the random variable $Z = (M, T,
X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$ for $p$. Writing $\mathrm{TV}$ for the total variation distance, the
quantity
\[
\mathrm{TV}\bigl(\mathrm{Law}(X_T \mid Z = z),\; \mathrm{Unif}\{0,1\}\bigr),
\]
the total variation distance between the conditional law of Alice's bit at the special
coordinate given $Z = z$ and the uniform distribution on one bit, is nonnegative.
